Hi Elena —

Following up with details on our evidence and retention options. Short answers up front: we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering mid-2024 through mid-2025; we can provide a customer-facing summary and a bridge letter where controls haven't materially changed. For logs and retention: 

- Hosted default retention: 90 days for request/response telemetry and 365 days for critical audit events.
- Extended retention: we offer export options to customer-managed S3 (recommended) or a dedicated retention bucket on Redwood Dedicated for up to 7 years (requires an add-on).
- KMS: you can use your own KMS for the S3 export; we support AWS KMS key policies.

For audit samples we will: 
- Provide redacted authentication and admin activity logs (JSONL), showing timestamps, user IDs (redacted), and event types.
- Provide an onboarding doc that maps our controls to typical customer controls (control matrix).
- Offer scoped, timeboxed access to logs via secure SFTP or a temporary read-only console role for your auditors (2-week window).

Risks / notes: if HealthLytics requires 7-year on-platform retention within a hosted model, that will require either: 1) a Dedicated retention add-on or 2) continuous log export to your S3 with your KMS. The S3 export is the more cost-effective and auditable route.

Please confirm which approach you prefer (export to your S3 + KMS OR Redwood Dedicated retention). Once confirmed, we’ll queue the export flow (estimate 5 business days to provision) and include the retention amendment in the SOW.

Thanks —
